summary: Károly Fiók was an Indologist who studied at Eötvös Loránd University, Berlin, Munich, and Kölcsey Ferenc Teacher Training College. He taught at Budapest Reformed High School (1886–1907) and served as a Latin teacher at Debrecen Reformed College (1907–1915).
Käthe Marschner was an Indologist who completed her PhD at the University of Breslau in 1933 under the supervision of Otto Strauss.

Käthe Neumann studied religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies at Greifswald, Berlin, and Marburg, completing her PhD under Johannes Nobel in 1933. She served as curator in charge at the Religionskundliche Sammlung from 1937 to 1968.

Kārlis Augusts Tennisons was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Saint Petersburg State University and taught Friedrich V. Lustig. He served as director of Datsan Gunzechoinei from 1906 to 1923.

Kōgi Kudara worked in Buddhist studies, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He served as a professor at Ryukoku University (~1978–2004) and held an editorial post at the Ryukoku Buddhist Society (attested 2002).
Kōichi Kozaka is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Hakuyu Hadano. He was a professor at Osaka Kyoiku University, attested in 1991.

Kōsen Imakita was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied under Kyokuso Hirose, Togai Fujisawa, Daisetsu Jōen, and Gisan Zenkai. He served as abbot at Eikō-ji (1858) and Engaku-ji (1875–1892), and as a Ministry of Religion Doctrinal Instructor (~1872–1877).
Kōshō Ōtani, who succeeded Kozui Otani, was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the First Higher School (~1929–1932) and Tokyo Imperial University (~1932–1935).

L. Johannes Frohnmeyer was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the Basel Mission (~1872–1876). He later served as inspector of missions at the Basel Mission (1876–1905) and was a Fellow of the University of Madras.

L. P. N. Perera worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as a supervisor at Vidyodaya Campus, University of Sri Lanka, and as Director of the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies.

Lajos Ligeti was a Central Asian, Tibetan, and Sinological scholar who studied at Eötvös Loránd University, Eötvös József Collegium, and Paris. He taught Mongolian (1931) and was Professor of Central Asian Languages (1940–1974) at Eötvös Loránd University.
Lajos Lóczy studied at the University of Zurich and ETH Zurich. He worked at the Hungarian National Museum in 1874 and was appointed Professor of Geography at Eötvös Loránd University in 1889.
Lak La Sönam Chö Drub studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.
Lakshman Sarup was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied under Arthur Anthony Macdonell. He served as University Professor of Sanskrit at Panjab University, attested in 1947.
Lakshmanacharya worked in Indology and philosophy, serving as a teacher at Shri Ramanuja Pathashala in Mathura (attested 1889 and 1900).
Lakshmi Swaminathan was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Queen Mary's College and Madras Medical College. She later served as a lecturer at Stony Brook University.

Lal Mani Joshi was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees at Allahabad, Banaras Hindu, and Gorakhpur. He held posts at Gorakhpur, Punjabi University, and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, alongside visiting appointments at Haverford and Amherst.
Lalchandra Bhagawandas Gandhi was an Indology scholar who served as Jain Pandit at the Central Library of Vadodara and held a post at the Oriental Institute, Vadodara (attested 1939).
Lama Jabb is a Tibetology scholar who served as a Junior Research Fellow at the University of Oxford and as Head of the Tibetan & Himalayan Studies Centre at Wolfson College, Oxford (attested 2026).

Lama Jampa Thaye is a Buddhist and Tibetan studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Manchester and studied with Karma Thinley Rinpoche and Sakya Trizin. He joined the teaching faculty at the Karmapa International Buddhist Institute.
